text: Searching online, you expect objective answers. Yet results often feel personal, shaped by past clicks. You seek neutral, unbiased information.
Frustrated, you open incognito. Retyping the query, you hope this 'private' mode reveals the true, unfiltered internet.
And often, you get different results! This makes you believe incognito grants complete anonymity and untraceable browsing.
Here's the system: incognito deletes *local* data, like cookies. It makes your browser act like a new user, with no past influencing the search.
The cost: incognito isn't total anonymity. It just removes your browser's *local memory* of you. Algorithms use a default profile, not hiding you.
So next time, you'll understand why incognito results shifted. It's not magic, but resetting the digital trail shaping your online world.
